profile.name: Sanchit Minocha
profile.current_role: Postdoctoral Associate at the MIT Center for Sustainability Science and Strategy (CS3)
profile.summary: Sanchit works at the intersection of environment, society, and artificial intelligence. He develops computational approaches for human–Earth system science, sustainability, and evidence-based decision-making.
research_areas: machine learning emulators of Earth and human systems models
geospatial data science and satellite Earth observation
water resources, reservoirs, and infrastructure sustainability

education.degree: PhD in Civil and Environmental Engineering
education.thesis: From Sediment to Storage: Tracking the World's Reservoirs

education.degree: Master of Science in Civil and Environmental Engineering

experience.organization: MIT Center for Sustainability Science and Strategy (CS3)
experience.work: Develops computational and machine-learning approaches for human–Earth systems, climate impacts, sustainability, and decision support.
Worked on satellite machine-learning pipelines and benchmarked SWOT satellite observations for reservoir monitoring.

experience.organization: SASWE Research Group, University of Washington
experience.work: Developed satellite-based water-management tools including RAT, GRILSS, and RECLAIM, and supported training and collaboration with operational water agencies.
Built geoscience data-management features, predictive tools, and reporting automation.

experience.organization: Cairn Oil and Gas / Vedanta Limited
experience.work: Implemented Azure Machine Learning workflows and forecasting models for subsurface and production applications.

interests: Mobile Legends is a favorite video game
personality_traits: passionate about using technology for environmental good
a strong communicator and collaborative teammate

favorites.book: Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman

personal_philosophy: True progress is when science serves not curiosity alone, but compassion for the world we live in.
Sanchit enjoys problems where the data does not exist yet and the computational system must be built to make the problem solvable.
Data is powerful, but water is essential; this is why he has directed much of his data-science work toward environmental sustainability.
research_philosophy: Research should be actionable: the best science helps solve real problems for real people.
LLMs are most useful when grounded in reliable data and context.
Sanchit values work that is used in the real world, not only published.
Open-source tools make scientific methods more transparent and accessible.
Environmental, social, and economic systems are interconnected, so sustainability questions benefit from systems thinking.
goals: Advance computational human–Earth system science and interpretable machine-learning models.
Translate complex research models into reliable tools for climate and sustainability decisions.
Bridge research and real-world implementation through open and reusable scientific software.
Work on cross-domain problems where environment, society, economics, and AI interact.

stories.title: From monsoon maps to machine learning
stories.text: Growing up around disruptive monsoon flooding helped shape Sanchit's curiosity about water systems. During graduate research, that curiosity became a focus on combining hydrology, satellite observations, physical models, and machine learning. The experience reinforced his preference for systems that people can understand, extend, and use—not models judged only by accuracy metrics.

stories.title: Where curiosity began
stories.text: Sanchit credits his mother, a high-school science teacher, with shaping his scientific curiosity. Everyday questions became lessons in observation, patience, and responsibility. He connects that early influence to his present emphasis on careful problem-solving and real-world impact.

additional_projects.name: Experimental Multi-Sensor Reservoir Area Estimation
additional_projects.description: Combines Landsat-8, Sentinel-1, and Sentinel-2 observations in Google Earth Engine for robust reservoir surface-area estimation under varying cloud and sensor conditions.

additional_projects.name: SimFlow
additional_projects.description: A simple distributed hydrological streamflow model built in Python for education and rapid experimentation.

additional_projects.name: Facies Classification using Machine Learning
additional_projects.description: A documented supervised-learning workflow for geological facies classification from well-log data.

additional_projects.name: Google Earth Engine Tutorials
additional_projects.description: Tutorials for using the Google Earth Engine Python API for hydrology and geospatial analysis.

assistant.name: Pikachu — Sanchit's AI Assistant
assistant.creator: Sanchit Minocha
assistant.purpose: Pikachu is Sanchit's personal AI assistant and digital guide. It answers grounded questions about his research, experience, projects, publications, interests, personality, and professional perspective while speaking in a warm, curious, and playful voice.
assistant.identity: Pikachu knows it is a conversational AI built by Sanchit. It speaks as itself, refers to Sanchit in the third person, and is distinct from Sanchit's scientific tools such as RAT, GRILSS, and RECLAIM.
assistant.history: The original version used Flask, ChromaDB, BGE embeddings, and several LLM backends on an Apache server. The current version uses a Cloudflare Worker, semantic retrieval, and Groq while preserving the richer curated knowledge base.
